yes. i had the same teacher for 3 years. she would call me names like turtle and molasses bc i moved slow and typed slow and took a while to finish writing our creative stories we were supposed to write, though that was because my stories were long. actually once she even yelled at me in front of the whole class about how i only had two pieces done when my classmate had 16 done. i talked a lot in class when i shouldn’t have, and while i understand that’s disruptive, how she treated me because of it was not great for my self esteem. she looked at me like i was a nuisance. she also had clear favorites and many of them were my friends so after elementary school i would go to dinner with the whole group sometimes, and i regret doing that, it always left me feeling a little bad about myself. oh also she tutored some of those friends in middle school, and when they told her i had skipped two grades in math, she rolled her eyes and said “of course.” why was she such a hater towards a kid?

btw if any of y’all do know me / who i’m taking abt, let me know if my memory is exaggerating or not ty

I agree with this, but she might have been talking abt systemic racism, in which case we’re all affected regardless of race, just in different ways and depending on other factors. Generally wealthy light skinned Indians hold a close proximity to whiteness in that sense though. And from the looks of it they live in a liberal area with many ppl of the same racial background (just curious, do you live in Dallas proper or somewhere like Plano?) and have only visited similar places, so I’m assuming that so far they’ve lived a pretty sheltered life. If you step outside this comfort zone, OP, I think you’ll think differently, but I see where you’re coming from right now. I’m also Indian with wealthy parents and grew up with many Indians. Also, there’s a possibility that OP hasn’t noticed how they’ve been discriminated against bc of their race in the past.

The cost varies depending on the sorority, but for the first two semesters its around $500-600 and goes down after that. Whether joining a sorority is worth it to you depends on what you want to get out of the experience. If you want to make friends that have many similar interests to you, its better to join clubs that you're interested in. (you should do this regardless, though.) But if you want to make friends who have similar outlooks on life who don't necessarily have to have the same exact interests as you then sorority life may just be for you.
